earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description for Kuuk-Yak is a wordlist or less only (Allen Hall 1968); no grammar/phonology exists

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter John. 1978. Wik: Aboriginal society, territory and language at Cape Keerweer, Cape York Peninsula, Australia. PhD thesis, University of Queensland. xii+368 pp. (ANU Open Research 1885/307607, Open Access scan + text).
sources.note: Nothing about Kuuk Yak; the thesis's linguistic content concerns Wik varieties.

sources.citation: Hall, Allen Harry. 1969 [1968]. A depth-study of the Thaayorr language of the Edward River tribe, Cape York Peninsula: being a description of the phonology with a brief grammatical outline and samples of lexicon and oral literature. M.A. thesis, University of Queensland, 352 pp. - esp. pp. 251-270 (Thaayorr-Kuuk Yak diglot comparison) and pp. 308-329 (discussion: 'salient phonological features').
sources.note: The only first-hand document with Kuuk Yak data that Glottolog knows (Glottolog's most extensive description source); its discussion section on 'salient phonological features' of the Yak comparison is the one place a stress remark on Kuuk Yak could exist. eSpace marks the PDF open (publisher version) but download is captcha-gated by automated download; a browser download should work.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Kuuk Yak language' and 'Kuuk Thaayorre language', raw wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Nothing on Kuuk Yak phonology. 'Very little is known about the language.. Barry Alpher is currently trying to collect all these pieces and fragments of information for his lexicon and grammar of the language' (cited to Austlang Y200 / Gaby 2017).

sources.citation: AIATSIS. Austlang: Y200 Kuuk Yak (full language page: names, comment, references, speaker table, Documentation table, classifications). Canberra: AIATSIS. Read from the Internet Archive capture of 2024-12-12 (web.archive.org/web/20241212005905/https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/Y200).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. Documentation table: Word list None, Text Collection None, Grammar None, Audio-visual None (AIATSIS holds no Kuuk Yak documentation as of the 2024 capture). Comment: 'According to Alpher (1972) and Gaby (2006), Kuku Yak and Thayore Y69 are closely related. Alpher's later studies of Kuuk-Yak (2006 p.c.) concludes that they are in fact not closely related.' References: Alpher 1972 (OL 11), Gaby 2006 (both round-1 works). Dixon (2002): 'Kuuk Thaayorre Hall (1972) further dialects: Yak, Kirka, Thayem, Thayunth'. Links to an Oates 1975 extract that is an automated-access bloc…

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter, Ken Hale & David Nash et al. 2021. Linguistic Organisation and Native Title: The Wik Case, Australia. Canberra: ANU Press (OAPEN).
sources.note: Nothing on Kuuk Yak; sole hit is a map legend '34 KUUK-YAK' (Walsh 1981-83 language-countries map). Stress remarks in the book concern Wik languages only.

sources.citation: Pama Language Centre. 2018. Kuuk Yak (language variety page, Cape York Peninsula languages map). Cairns: Pama Language Centre.https://www.pamacentre.org.au/kuuk-yak/(posted 17 April 2018; read 2026-09-21).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing. 'This language variety currently does not receive Pama Language Centre support.. summary information for this language which has been assembled by the Cape York Peninsula Languages Survey. The table below will be updated with this information soon.' All sections (phonemic transcription 'Hyperlink to a webpage with a phonology chart', Linguistic notes & sources, Dictionary 'WATCH THIS SPACE', Open access archival resources) are placeholder instructions; no wordlist, recording, orthography or source is listed.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-101 and New Code Request form for [uky] Kuuk-Yak (A. Aristar / MultiTree, supported by C. Bowern). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. States (sec. 4a) 'No written literature or recordings exist, and AIATSIS does not hold any documentation'; extinct per Austlang/Wurm; Oates 1975 estimated 40 speakers.

sources.citation: Hall, Allen Harry. 1972. A study in the Thaayorre language of the Edward River tribe, Cape York Peninsula, Queensland: being a description of the grammar. PhD thesis, University of Queensland (2 vols).
sources.note: Hall's fuller Thaayorre grammar from the same Edward River fieldwork; may repeat or extend the Kuuk Yak comparison and dialect notes (Yak listed among 'dialects represented at Edward River' in the 1968 thesis).

sources.citation: Jones, Audrey M. 1972. Australian Institute of Aboriginal Studies: Catalogue of Tape Archive, No. 9. Canberra: AIAS (ERIC microfiche, archive.org micro_IA41153637_0648).
sources.note: Nothing. Lists Hall tapes A562/A563 (Brisbane 1966): talk in Thaayorre about 'home and language of the Kuuk Yak (Snake language) people' - recordings about, not in or describing, Kuuk Yak.

sources.citation: AIATSIS. Austlang dataset (open-data extract), record Y200 'Kuuk Yak' (synonyms Yak, Kuuku Yak, Koko Yak; -14.877, 141.732). data.gov.au package 'austlang-dataset-001', datastore resource e9a9ea06-d821-4b53-a05f-877409a1a19c.

sources.citation: Hammarstrom et al. Glottolog 5.3, languoid kuuk1243 Kuuk-Yak (page + local glottolog-cldf 5.1 /sources.bib).
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist; sole descriptive ref is Hall 1968 'Diglot linguistic comparison' pp. 251-270 (listed by Glottolog as a wordlist); other refs are ISO CR, Ethnologue, Austlang.

sources.citation: Gaby, Alice R. 2017. A Grammar of Kuuk Thaayorre (Mouton Grammar Library 74). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Ch. 1 Introduction (section on neighbouring languages/dialects incl. Kuuk Yak) and ch. 2 Phonology.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Authoritative modern statement of what is and is not known about Kuuk Yak and its relation to Kuuk Thaayorre (dialect vs sister language); needed for the identity note and to confirm that no Kuuk Yak phonology is given. (2006 PhD version: hdl.handle.net/11343/39145, currently withdrawn from Minerva.)

sources.citation: Alpher, Barry & David Nash. 1999. Lexical replacement and cognate equilibrium in Australia. Australian Journal of Linguistics 19(1): 5-56.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Cites Kuuk-Yak (KYak) forms from Alpher's own data; its source note would identify what Kuuk Yak corpus Alpher held by 1999. Not expected to state stress.

sources.citation: Alpher, Barry. n.d. (2000s-). Kuuk Yak field notes, recordings and draft lexicon/grammar (salvage work with rememberers at Pormpuraaw); any AIATSIS deposit under Austlang Y200.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Wikipedia/Gaby 2017 report Alpher compiling a Kuuk Yak lexicon and grammar; if a sketch exists (published or deposited) it would be the only modern description and would supersede Hall 1968. Check Austlang Y200 'documentation' table and AIATSIS Mura catalogue, or ask Alpher/Bowern directly (Bowern co-sponsored the ISO code request).

sources.citation: Verstraete, Jean-Christophe & Diane Hafner (eds.). 2016. Land and Language in Cape York Peninsula and the Gulf Country (Culture and Language Use 18). Amsterdam: John Benjamins. Chapter list via Crossref; incl. Alpher, 'Connecting Thaypanic'; Gaby, 'Hyponymy and the structure of Kuuk Thaayorre kinship'.
